//PartnerAuth: Issuer must be this service's public origin: partners target it as the 'aud' of their
assertions, and it is stamped as 'iss' on every token we mint. Changing it invalidates every
token in flight and every assertion partners are currently building.
//Partners: Partner registrations. Nothing here is secret: a client id, a display name, the partner's
PUBLIC signing key, and a scope grant. Partners sign with the matching private key, which
never leaves them, so there is no shared credential to distribute or rotate in lockstep.

PublicKeyPem is a PEM-encoded RSA or ECDSA public key. In JSON, write newlines as 
.
Reconciliation is additive: a registration present here is created or updated, one that is
absent is left alone. Silently orphaning a partner's worker links on a config typo would be
worse than leaving a stale row. Set Active:false for the kill switch.
The admin API that replaces this file is phase 3e.
//PracticeManager: The gRPC endpoint of PracticeManager.Api, and the shared key it expects as x-api-key.
The key is a secret and comes from the environment (PracticeManager__ApiKey).
PushTimeout is generous because a cold push does a real browser login against Xero's bot
//Reconciler: Owns retrying the push. PracticeManager.Api has no job queue by design - the caller already
holds a durable record of what needs syncing - so this service is that record.
Statements are pushed strictly one at a time: PM is a single browser session behind a queue
of one, so concurrency here would only move the queue upstream.
AwaitingStatementInterval is hours because nothing we do makes the ATO issue a statement
sooner, and every check costs a session slot a real push could have used.
//Webhooks: Outbound status webhooks. Optional per partner - a partner with no WebhookUrl simply polls,
and polling works throughout, so a webhook that never arrives never blocks a lodgement.
Delivery is at least once: every request carries an X-Bas-Delivery id to deduplicate on.
Signed with HMAC-SHA256 over 'timestamp.payload' in X-Bas-Signature. A shared secret is
appropriate here in a way it is not on the token endpoint: leaking it lets someone send a
partner a false status update, not mint tokens for any worker.
//Admin: The admin surface: a Blazor console at /admin and a REST surface at /admin/v1.
The default account below is seeded on every fresh database, matching the other tools in the
practice. Seeding is create-only: an existing account is never updated from here, so changing
the password in configuration does nothing once it has been created.
Two-factor is available per account but not enforced.
Keys are for scripts and runbooks. The NAME is not a secret and is what the audit log records,
so give each caller its own rather than sharing one. No keys and no users means nobody can
reach the admin surface at all, which is the correct default.
Override per environment with Admin__Users__0__Email / Admin__Users__0__InitialPassword.
Keys are never committed - they come from Admin__Keys__0__Key.
//Cors: Origins our JS is embedded on, i.e. the partner's web app. Credentials are deliberately NOT
allowed: bearer tokens mean no ambient cookie travels, which is the point of the design.
An empty list means no cross-origin caller, not 'allow everyone'.
